beats.act: Open the Library
beats.say: The Library is the parts bin: skills, hooks, connections, templates, and what the community has published.

beats.act: Press "+ New skill"
beats.say: A skill is a reusable instruction packet — the unit an agent composes to know how to do something.

beats.act: Describe the skill to the creation agent instead of writing the package by hand
beats.say: This is the fork in the road, and both branches are real: the operator can type the package into the form beside this one, or describe what they want and let the creation agent draft it.

beats.act: Open the authoring session it just started
beats.say: Forge mints the session and says so on the page the operator is already standing on, rather than moving them somewhere they did not ask to go.

beats.act: Read what it drafted, give the package its directory name, and approve it
beats.say: The agent drafts; the operator names and approves.

beats.act: Trust it: approve the draft in the library
beats.say: Two approvals, because they answer different questions.

beats.act: Go back to the Library
beats.say: The Library is where the operator returns between kinds.

beats.act: Press "+ New hook"
beats.say: A hook is the other kind of part: not instructions but a script, run on an agent’s lifecycle event.

beats.act: Write the hook by hand: what it runs on, what it does, and what it may touch
beats.say: The permissions fields are the operator declaring, up front, what this script is allowed to reach.

beats.act: Read the security scan before trusting it
beats.say: This is the gate that exists because a hook runs with the operator’s own credentials.

beats.act: Check what is actually in the package — every file, and the fingerprint over all of them
beats.say: Approving bytes you were never shown is not approving.

beats.act: Approve the hook
beats.say: Trust and verdict are two different axes, and this is the trust one.

beats.act: Test-fire the approved hook, before any agent carries it
beats.say: Approval is a promise about bytes; a test-fire is the bytes running.

beats.act: Go back to the Library once more
beats.say: Third kind, same parts bin.

beats.act: Press "+ New template" and write the template the hook’s output is filed into
beats.say: A template is one markdown definition file — the shape an artifact comes out in.

beats.act: Back to the Library
beats.say: Instructions are the fourth kind of part, and their door now sits in the parts bin with the other three.

beats.act: Open the instructions launcher straight from the Library
beats.say: One click from the parts bin to the launcher.

beats.act: Draft the project’s own working instructions, so the parts have a house style to follow
beats.say: Instructions are the fourth kind of component and the only one that is about the project rather than about forge: the AGENTS.md every agent dispatched at this repo reads before it does anything.

beats.act: Open the instructions session it just started
beats.say: Same shape as the skill: forge mints the session and says so where the operator already is, and reaching it is their own next act.

beats.act: Head back to the Agents pillar
beats.say: The parts are all made now — a skill, a hook, a template, a house style.

beats.act: Open brain-ingest from the roster
beats.say: The roster is a list of workers; binding happens on one worker’s own page.

beats.act: Bind the hook to the agent, and save it
beats.say: A hook is inert until an agent carries it.

beats.act: Run the agent
beats.say: The hook is bound, so this run is the first time anything other than the operator can set it off.

beats.act: Wait for the run to end
beats.say: A session that ends is the event this hook was written for.

beats.act: Back to the Library
beats.say: The record of what a hook did lives with the hook, not with whichever agent happened to trigger it.

beats.act: Open the hook, and see the session ending fire it
beats.say: This is where S7 ends: the hook the operator wrote, scanned, approved and bound actually ran, and its own page says when and how it ended.
